source.title: Next-Scale Autoregressive Models are Zero-Shot Single-Image Object View Synthesizers

record.file_problem: The paper text is complete. Figures 7 and 8 are referenced, but their plotted values are not available in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Applies next-scale autoregression in image-based novel-view synthesis and reports its own model- and dataset-size scaling results, but does not test language-model cross-entropy scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper reports NVS performance trends with model and dataset size. It does not report held-out cross-entropy, fit a power law, test prediction from smaller runs, or investigate compute-optimal allocation. Benchmark comparisons and architectural ablations are not scaling results.
record.test_reason: The study trains next-scale autoregressive image models for novel-view synthesis at five depths and on subsampled datasets, and reports how performance scales (Figs. 7–8). This is a new modality bearing on V5. It reports no loss curves, no power-law fits and no compute axis, so the evidence is qualitative.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say performance scales with model and dataset size, with preliminary scaling-law-like behaviour below 1B parameters. They say larger models are likely bottlenecked by dataset size, and more data (beyond Objaverse's 800k objects) should help further.
record.recipe_differences: This is an image-based novel-view-synthesis study using a next-scale autoregressive model and NVS performance measures, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling-law fits.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors identify dataset size as a likely bottleneck for larger models.
record.problems: The scaling evidence is described as preliminary; the paper does not provide fitted power-law exponents or numerical scaling results in the supplied text. It reports five repetitions with standard-deviation error bars. Compute scaling is not evaluated.

untested.parts: No extrapolation from small fitted runs.
No compute-optimal allocation; compute scaling explicitly not considered.
Width fixed at 64×depth; no shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No fitted power-law form or exponents. No loss measure, compute axis, video, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
No relation between pretraining loss and downstream metrics.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Time-vs-PSNR plots for models scaled to different parameter sizes on each benchmark. This is an additional model-size result, though the values are unreadable in the text.
Exact metric (likely PSNR) and dataset subset sizes for the scaling sweeps. Needed to check the curve form.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label is dropped. Flattening above 1B is attributed to a data bottleneck, which matches the power-law claim's own condition that the other factors not be bottlenecks; it is not a qualification of V5. Benchmark and ablation tables are not scaling results. Fig. 1 reportedly compares ArchonView models at several parameter sizes, but no row captures it (see missing).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss and power-law dependence on parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation; the paper explicitly does not consider scaling with computation.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study reports image-task performance scaling, not a fitted power law in held-out loss; it does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream-task performance as a function of pretraining loss or scale.
Sensitivity of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations to setup or fitting choices.

rows.subject: ArchonView model-size scaling sweep
rows.size_stated: Five model depths: 12, 16, 20, 24, and 30; parameter counts not stated for the sweep.
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size and measured NVS performance.
rows.measure: NVS performance; exact plotted metric values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.value: The authors report preliminary evidence of scaling-law-like behavior below 1B parameters; they say larger models are likely bottlenecked by dataset size.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 7 error bars are ± one standard deviation from five repetitions each.
rows.note: The reported result is a qualitative image-task scaling trend, not a fitted power law in held-out loss. Individual plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.
rows.check: Measure is an NVS image-quality metric (Fig. 7 values unreadable), not held-out loss, and no power law is fitted. Authors claim 'scaling law-like behavior below 1B parameters'. Depth 24 is the 1.0B model, so only the depth-30 point is above 1B, where gains flatten. Width is tied to depth (64×), so this is a size sweep, not a shape test (V4).

rows.subject: ArchonView dataset-size scaling sweep
rows.size_stated: Dataset subsets sampled from Objaverse; subset sizes not stated.
rows.operation_detail: Trained models using randomly subsampled training-set objects and measured NVS performance.
rows.measure: NVS performance; exact plotted metric values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.value: The authors say that adding more data would likely continue to improve performance considerably.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 8 error bars are ± one standard deviation from five repetitions each.
rows.note: This is a qualitative dataset-size trend, not a fitted power law in held-out loss. Individual plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.
rows.check: Authors only say more data would likely keep improving performance. Subset sizes, metric values and curve form are not given, so the power-law form V5 names cannot be read. The row shows monotone improvement at most.

relationships.condition: ArchonView NVS model-size sweep, depths 12–24 (≤1B parameters)
relationships.reason: Authors report 'scaling law-like behavior below 1B parameters' on NVS performance (r1). This is weak support: no fit, no loss, and plotted values are unreadable.
relationships.display_finding: The authors reported scaling-law-like view synthesis performance below 1B parameters, without a fitted law or loss measurements.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
